summary: B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the requested convenience API using the established multipart helper without changing global retry behavior. Both patches improperly duplicate FilesService.Add instead of delegating to it, but A additionally makes a broad, explicitly prohibited change to RawClient request-body semantics.
reasons: B keeps the implementation narrowly scoped to FilesService.Upload and reuses multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and filename.

A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every io.Reader unless WithNoRetry is present, affecting unrelated endpoints, upload sizes, read-error timing, and streaming semantics; the contract explicitly forbids refactoring unrelated retry machinery.

Both Upload implementations call Raw.Do and duplicate Add's option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating a direct contract requirement.
A's added Add/os.File retry behavior and Files.Update changelog claim exceed the requested scope and conflict with preserving Add's existing behavior as the lower-level API.
risks_a: Global buffering can unexpectedly consume large or unbounded readers into memory, even outside FilesService and even when a retry policy will not actually retry.
Upload bypasses Add, creating duplicate machinery that can drift from Add's future behavior.
The changelog and README advertise broader behavioral changes that the frozen contract explicitly excludes.
risks_b: Upload bypasses Add rather than delegating to it, so option, response, and error behavior are only duplicated rather than guaranteed to remain unified.
Tests omit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases required by the contract.

The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods as in the reported scenario or verify that the complete streamed payload arrives on every attempt; it only counts requests and checks the final response exposure.
